living.label: A living giant the spell really hurts
living.explanation: A Necromancer considers Dispel Life against a hill giant five grids away. The game's drain hits living monsters: a native cast removes 66 HP. The original rating keeps damage only for monsters flagged both nonliving and undead — no monster in the game data has the nonliving flag — so the spell is valued below doing nothing. The correction rates it like the game: the launch value minus the mana cost of the spell.

undead.label: Control: an undead bat the spell cannot hurt
undead.explanation: A vampire bat is explicitly undead, and the game's drain leaves it untouched (native cast removes nothing). Both versions refuse the cast; only the raw number of the refusal differs. The corrected rating applies the chooser's standing mana penalty to a zero-damage launch instead of a dead filter.
